title: The CLI renders markdown in bodies, notes and memories
body:
The screen renders a body through `md::render` in `src/md.rs`. The CLI does not. `render::issue` in `src/render.rs` prints the body with `Style::wrapped(&i.body, 0, 0)` and each note the same way under a hanging indent. `render::memory` and `render::memories` print memory text the same way. `Style::wrapped` returns the text untouched when `human` is false, which `Style::detect` sets for a pipe, `--plain` and `--json`. On a terminal it calls `wrap_at`, which keeps line breaks and collapses every run of whitespace to one space.

So the markdown that `foam prime` asks an agent to write comes out as its source characters. On a terminal it comes out worse than the source: a fence loses its indentation, a table loses its column spacing, and a long bullet wraps without a hanging indent.

The commands that print this text:

| command | function | text |
|---|---|---|
| `foam show` | `render::issue` | body and notes |
| `foam recall` | `render::memory` | one memory |
| `foam memories` | `render::memories` | one line per memory |
| `foam search` | `render::memories` | memory hits |
| `foam prime` | `prime.rs` | memories, raw |

## Proposal

- A function in `md.rs` that lays out blocks for a terminal rather than the screen, along the lines of `md::text(text: &str, width: usize, color: bool) -> String`. It reuses `parse` and the width logic in `layout`, and emits ANSI only when `color` is set.
- `render::issue` and `render::memory` call it when `human` is set, at `style.width` less the hang, and indent each line by the hang. The `Paragraph`, `List`, `Code`, `Table` and `Heading` blocks all render. Headers come from foam-a24c63, which this issue waits on.
- Piped, `--plain` and `--json` output stay the raw markdown. A program reading foam wants the source.
- `foam prime` stays raw. The agent reads markdown.

## Open

- What `foam memories` does with a memory that holds a fence or a table. The listing is one line per memory, and a table does not fit on one line. Rendering only inline code there and leaving blocks to `foam recall` is one answer.
- Whether `foam search` shows the matching body or note under an issue hit. Today it shows title rows only, so there is nothing to render.
close_reason: Landed in commit bb756ff, 'Render markdown in show, recall and memories on a terminal'. Note 1 has the layout decisions.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/f1b5fba8
notes.text: A note that renders to one line that fits after its header stays on that line, as before. One that renders to more than one line, or to a line too long for the room after the header, goes under the header at the thread's indent. A fence or a bullet cannot start after the header, and rendering the first line narrower than the rest would need a second width through the layout. The memories listing renders every block under the slug column at the width less the column, so a table in a memory comes out as a table; the open question about that listing is answered that way. `foam search` still shows title rows only.
